newsitem.title: UK: Guinness confident of merger clearance.
newsitem.headline: Guinness confident of merger clearance.

text.p: British drinks group Guinness Plc is confident that its proposed merger with Grand Metropolitan Plc will be cleared by the authorities, chairman Tony Greener told shareholders, who packed the aisles at the group's annual meeting.
"Naturally the board looked at it in the greatest detail and we would not have gone ahead if we did not think we could consummate this merger," said Greener.
Guinness and GrandMet unveiled a 23 billion stg merger on Monday aimed at tackling difficult conditions in a fragmented market by creating the world's leading spirits and wine company.
"The range of brands are highly complementary," Greener told shareholders. He said that both groups had remarkably different brands with very few overlaps.
"When put together we represent only about five percent of the world spirits market," he said.
"So we do not think it will be a major issue, and the board is confident it will be cleared."
The planned merger has drawn complaints from rival Seagram Co Ltd, who claim that the merger would represent unfair competition in the U.S.
The European Commission has also been notified of the planned merger.
